plate_findings.evidence: Sagittal T2-weighted image showing cerebellar atrophy

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Sagittal T2-weighted brain MRI from an adult patient with NPC demonstrating cerebellar atrophy, a classic manifestation of the disease. B: Axial T1-weighted brain MRI from an adult NPC patient showing frontal atrophy with ex-vacuo ventricular dilation, consistent with disease-related cortical atrophy. C: Axial T2-weighted brain MRI from an adult NPC patient showing combined bilateral temporal and cerebellar atrophy, representing characteristic disease involvement. D: Axial T2-weighted brain MRI from an adult NPC patient demonstrating cerebellar atrophy, a hallmark radiological finding in this disease. E: Axial T1-weighted brain MRI from an adult NPC patient showing cerebellar atrophy, confirming the characteristic neurodegenerative pattern. F: Axial FLAIR brain MRI from an adult NPC patient showing cortical atrophy, representing the diffuse cerebral involvement typical of the disease.
panels.attribution_text: Devaraj et al. Spectrum of Movement Disorders in Niemann-Pick Disease Type C.. Tremor and other hyperkinetic movements (New York, N.Y.) 2022. doi:10.5334/tohm.701. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.

in_text_mentions: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was done in 8 patients. Diffuse cerebral and cerebellar atrophy was seen in 6 patients. Two patients with late-infantile onset had signal change in periventricular white matter with bilateral fronto-temporal atrophy (Figures 1 & 2). Computed tomography of the head was done in one patient with juvenile-onset and showed cerebellar atrophy.

findings.label: Vertical supranuclear gaze palsy
findings.evidence: The patient's clinical appearance at 11 years of age included neuropsychomotor delay, dystonic posture of the hands and feet, and vertical supranuclear gaze palsy (VSGP).

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of an 11-year-old patient with Niemann-Pick disease type C. The caption explicitly documents vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, a classic finding for NPC, as part of the patient's clinical appearance in this figure. The image also visibly demonstrates dystonic posture of the hands and feet, consistent with the disease.
